title: Learn Not the Way of the Nations
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: The news cycle feeds an endless cycle of fear. Christians are not to be ruled by fear or swayed by headlines. Look to the Savior who has won.
exhortation: I don't know about you, but I can get into a cycle of news listening that becomes a bombardment. We live in an information age: you can know anything happening in any country in the world, and sometimes you're expected to. "Did you hear about that thing in that place?" "No, I didn't," and now I feel like I need to know. Most of it is bad news, and a lot of it is fear.

If we're not careful, it becomes an endless cycle of fear, where every day we're looking for the latest thing to be afraid of and shrink back from. I think that's very much a work of the enemy. It's where he wants us to live. And if that characterizes how we approach our day, it's probably more a sign of the nations' influence on our thinking than of biblical thinking.

As Christians, that is not how we operate. We are not to be ruled by fear or swayed by headlines. This world and all the terrible things going on in it should not affect us the way they affect the nations. 2 Timothy 1:7 says, "For God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power and love and self-control." That is the heart posture of the Christian. A spirit of fear can't live at ease in the same heart as a spirit of power, love and a sound mind. They will go to war.

That's why I need the gospel every morning. I need to be reminded of my Savior and his finished work, when he said, "It is finished." We have a Savior who is fully trustworthy. Through every circumstance we can look to our risen, conquering Savior, who graciously laid out the whole future for us: what will happen, and that he will return and restore all things. Not one injustice will go unnoticed when he returns. He will set it all right, and we can trust that. So let's lift our eyes this morning. Let's not look to the nations and the fear cycle they live in, but to Jesus, who has won the victory for us.
prayer: Lord, all that we need is in you. You have provided all we need: food, clothes, physical protection and spiritual protection. And in your death on the cross, our greatest need was met. Sin clung so close it was part of us, and you removed it. Through the power of your blood shed for us, you gave us a new heart, new life, a hope and a future.

May we put our full trust in you today. Let us not look to our own strength, ingenuity or plans, or to our job or our money, but to you, who graciously provide all those things. Be with us today. We pray against anxiety and fear. Whatever news comes out, whatever the next big thing is, may we look to you and find comfort and peace in your sovereign hand. In Jesus' name, amen.
